method: A heat transfer coefficient, or U-value, is the heat flow through a unit area per kelvin of temperature difference: watts per square metre-kelvin, the base unit here. Every listed unit is reduced to that base by one definitional factor. Watt per square metre-degree Celsius equals watt per square metre-kelvin because a temperature difference of one degree Celsius is one kelvin, and the kilowatt unit is 1000 times the watt unit. The imperial units use the International Table Btu of exactly 1055.05585262 J, 3600 s per hour, 0.3048 m per foot (a square foot is 0.09290304 m²) and a temperature interval of 5/9 K per degree Fahrenheit: Btu/(h·ft²·°F) is 5.67826334111349 W/(m²·K), and the same Btu per hour-square foot over a Celsius interval is 3.15459074506305 W/(m²·K). The Celsius heat unit is exactly 1.8 Btu, the heat that raises one pound of water by one degree Celsius, so CHU/(h·ft²·°F) is 10.2208740140043 W/(m²·K). The calorie-based units use the thermochemical calorie of exactly 4.184 J: kcal/(h·m²·°C) is 4184/3600 = 1.16222222222222 W/(m²·K) and cal/(s·cm²·°C) is 4.184/0.0001 = 41840 W/(m²·K). A conversion multiplies by the source factor and divides by the target factor, so every ordered pair round trips. The reciprocal of the imperial result is reported as an R-value in h·ft²·°F/Btu, the US convention; layers of a wall add their imperial R-values in series before the sum is inverted again. Input is trimmed and must be a plain decimal, optionally with grouped thousands; a leading decimal point is accepted, exponent form is refused, and values below zero or above 1,000,000 W/(m²·K) are rejected with the reason. Results carry six significant digits with ties away from zero, trailing zeros trimmed, thousands grouped, and magnitudes outside 1e-6 to 1e12 in exponential form. Everything runs in the browser; nothing is uploaded, stored or sent anywhere.
